test_cases.test_name: Verify Continuous Temperature Monitoring and Recording Intervals
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS continuously monitors temperature in GMP storage areas and records readings at intervals not exceeding 5 minutes.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are calibrated and operational.
Access to EMS software and data logs.

test_steps.action: Observe the EMS software interface for a designated GMP storage area.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS displays real-time temperature readings for the selected storage area.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of EMS interface showing real-time temperature.

test_steps.action: Access the historical data logs for the same storage area over a period of at least 15 minutes.
test_steps.expected_result: Temperature readings are recorded at intervals of 5 minutes or less.
data_to_capture: Exported data log showing timestamps and temperature readings.

acceptance_criteria: Real-time temperature is continuously displayed.
All recorded temperature data points are within 5-minute intervals.
data_integrity_requirements: Data is recorded accurately and without loss.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Temperature Alarm Generation and Notification
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS generates alerts when temperature deviates ±2°C from setpoint and that alarm notifications integrate with the site paging system.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are calibrated and operational.
Defined setpoints and alarm thresholds are configured.
Site paging system is operational and configured for integration.
Access to EMS software and alarm logs.

test_steps.action: Adjust the temperature in a monitored storage area to intentionally trigger a high-temperature alarm (e.g., +2°C above setpoint).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS generates a visual and audible alarm within the system interface.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of EMS interface showing active alarm.
Timestamp of alarm generation.

test_steps.action: Verify that an alarm notification is sent to the site paging system.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm notification is received on the designated paging device.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of received page (e.g., screenshot of message, log entry).
Timestamp of notification.

test_steps.action: Return the temperature to within the acceptable range.
test_steps.expected_result: The alarm condition is cleared in the EMS and the paging system.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of EMS interface showing cleared alarm.
Timestamp of alarm clearance.

test_steps.action: Repeat steps 1-3 for a low-temperature alarm condition (e.g., -2°C below setpoint).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS generates a visual and audible alarm, and a notification is sent to the site paging system, which then clears.
data_to_capture: Screenshots of EMS interface for low-temp alarm and clearance.
Timestamps for low-temp alarm generation, notification, and clearance.

acceptance_criteria: Temperature deviations trigger immediate alarms in the EMS.
Alarm notifications are successfully sent to the site paging system.
Alarm conditions are cleared upon return to normal temperature ranges.
Alarm response time does not exceed 30 seconds.
data_integrity_requirements: Alarm events are accurately logged with timestamps.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Temperature Accuracy and Range Compliance
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS accurately measures temperature within the specified range and meets the required accuracy.
prerequisites: EMS is installed and configured.
Calibrated temperature probes are available.
Access to the EMS software interface.

test_steps.action: Introduce calibrated temperature probes to a GMP storage area and set the temperature to the lower limit of the specified range (-80°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS displays the temperature reading within ±0.5°C of the actual setpoint.
data_to_capture: Actual temperature reading from calibrated probe.
Displayed temperature on EMS.
Timestamp of reading.

test_steps.action: Gradually increase the temperature to the upper limit of the specified range (+50°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS continuously displays temperature readings within ±0.5°C of the actual setpoint throughout the range.
data_to_capture: Actual temperature readings from calibrated probe at various points.
Displayed temperatures on EMS at various points.
Timestamps of readings.

test_steps.action: Set the temperature to a point within the specified range (e.g., 20°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS displays the temperature reading within ±0.5°C of the actual setpoint.
data_to_capture: Actual temperature reading from calibrated probe.
Displayed temperature on EMS.
Timestamp of reading.

acceptance_criteria: All temperature readings displayed by the EMS are within ±0.5°C of the actual temperature measured by the calibrated probe across the entire specified range (-80°C to +50°C).
data_integrity_requirements: Data captured must be accurate and traceable to calibrated equipment.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Data Storage and Archival Functionality
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS correctly stores all recorded data and that the archival feature functions as expected for long-term retention.
prerequisites: EMS is installed and configured.
Sufficient data has been generated to test archival (e.g., simulate several days of monitoring).
Access to EMS administration and archival functions.

test_steps.action: Monitor the EMS for a defined period (e.g., 24 hours) to generate a substantial amount of data.
test_steps.expected_result: All temperature and humidity readings are continuously recorded by the EMS at the specified intervals.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of continuous data recording.
Sample of recorded data points with timestamps.

test_steps.action: Access the vendor's standard database format and verify the integrity and completeness of the stored data for the monitored period.
test_steps.expected_result: The stored data is complete, accurate, and matches the recorded data within the EMS.
data_to_capture: Screenshots or export of stored data.
Comparison of stored data with EMS displayed data.

test_steps.action: Initiate the vendor's archival feature to archive data older than a specified period (e.g., 1 year, to simulate a portion of the 7-year requirement).
test_steps.expected_result: The archival process completes successfully, and the specified data is moved to the archive location.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of successful archival process.
Timestamp of archival initiation and completion.

test_steps.action: Attempt to retrieve archived data to verify its accessibility and integrity.
test_steps.expected_result: Archived data can be successfully retrieved and is identical to the data prior to archival.
data_to_capture: Screenshots or export of retrieved archived data.
Confirmation of data integrity after retrieval.

acceptance_criteria: All temperature and humidity data is continuously recorded and stored in the vendor's standard database format.
The archival feature successfully archives data, and archived data is retrievable and maintains its integrity.
Data retention meets the 7-year requirement through the archival mechanism.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 (implied by audit trail and retention requirements)
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be stored accurately and completely.
Archived data must be retrievable and unaltered.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Audit Trail and Electronic Signature Functionality for Data Modifications
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system generates a comprehensive audit trail for all data modifications and that electronic signatures are applied correctly as per 21 CFR Part 11.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
User accounts with appropriate permissions for data modification are available.
A known data point (e.g., a historical temperature reading) is identified for modification.

test_steps.action: Attempt to modify a historical temperature data point within the EMS system.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prompts for an electronic signature and provides a reason for the modification.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the modification prompt.
Details of the electronic signature entered.

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail for the attempted modification.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail records the user, date, time, action performed (modification), the original value, the new value, and the electronic signature with its associated reason.
data_to_capture: Audit trail log entries for the modification.
Screenshot of the audit trail report.

test_steps.action: Verify that the electronic signature meets 21 CFR Part 11 requirements (e.g., unique identifier, date/time, meaning of signature).
test_steps.expected_result: The electronic signature in the audit trail is complete and compliant with 21 CFR Part 11.
data_to_capture: Details of the electronic signature from the audit trail.

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully prompts for and captures an electronic signature for data modification.
The audit trail accurately records all details of the data modification, including user, timestamp, action, old value, new value, and electronic signature.
The electronic signature format complies with 21 CFR Part 11 requirements.
data_integrity_requirements: Audit trail must be complete, accurate, and secure.
Electronic signatures must be unique, attributable, and non-repudiable.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Integration with Facility Management and Paging Systems
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system can successfully interface with the existing facility management system and integrate alarm notifications with the site paging system.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Facility Management System (FMS) is operational and accessible.
Site Paging System is operational and accessible.
Vendor API for alarm notifications is available and documented.
Network connectivity between systems is established.

test_steps.action: Trigger a simulated alarm condition in the EMS system (e.g., by temporarily exceeding a temperature setpoint).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS system generates an alarm notification.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of alarm generation within EMS.
Timestamp of alarm generation.

test_steps.action: Verify that the alarm data is transmitted to the Facility Management System via standard protocols.
test_steps.expected_result: The FMS receives and logs the alarm event from the EMS system.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the alarm event in the FMS.
Timestamp of alarm reception in FMS.

test_steps.action: Verify that the alarm notification is sent to the site paging system using the vendor API.
test_steps.expected_result: An alert is received on the designated paging device(s) with relevant alarm information.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the alert on the paging device.
Timestamp of alert reception on paging device.

test_steps.action: Acknowledge the alarm in the EMS system and verify that the acknowledgment is reflected in the FMS and potentially the paging system (if applicable).
test_steps.expected_result: The alarm status is updated in all integrated systems.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of alarm acknowledgment in EMS.
Screenshot of updated alarm status in FMS.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS system successfully transmits alarm data to the FMS.
The EMS system successfully sends alarm notifications to the site paging system via the vendor API.
Alarm acknowledgments are correctly propagated across integrated systems.
data_integrity_requirements: Alarm data transmitted to FMS must be accurate and complete.
Alarm notifications to paging system must be timely and contain correct information.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Vendor Standard Reports for Batch Release
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system generates and provides standard reports as supplied by the vendor for use in batch release.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
Sufficient historical data exists to generate reports.
Access to vendor-supplied reporting tools is available.

test_steps.action: Access the reporting module of the EMS.
test_steps.expected_result: The reporting module is accessible and displays available report templates.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the reporting module interface.

test_steps.action: Select and generate a standard temperature report for a defined period (e.g., last 24 hours).
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates a temperature report in the vendor's standard format.
data_to_capture: Generated report file (e.g., PDF, CSV).
Screenshot of the generated report.

test_steps.action: Review the generated report for accuracy and completeness of data, ensuring it aligns with recorded temperature data.
test_steps.expected_result: The report accurately reflects the recorded temperature data for the specified period and includes all required fields as per vendor documentation.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of data accuracy in the report.

test_steps.action: Verify that the generated report is suitable for use in batch release decisions.
test_steps.expected_result: The report contains all necessary information (e.g., date, time, temperature values, alarm status) to support batch release.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of report suitability for batch release.

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully generates standard vendor reports.
Generated reports are accurate and complete.
Reports are in the vendor's standard format and suitable for batch release.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-007: Standard reports provided by vendor shall be used for batch release.
data_integrity_requirements: Data presented in reports must be accurate and traceable to raw data.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Availability and Response Time for Alarms
test_cases.objective: To verify that the Environmental Monitoring System meets the specified availability requirements and responds to alarm conditions within the defined time.
prerequisites: System is fully operational and monitored.
Alarm conditions can be simulated or are actively occurring.
Access to system logs and monitoring tools is available.

test_steps.action: Monitor system uptime over a defined period (e.g., 24 hours) and record any unplanned downtime.
test_steps.expected_result: The system remains operational for at least 99.5% of the monitored period, excluding scheduled maintenance.
data_to_capture: System uptime logs.
Record of any unplanned downtime incidents (start/end times, duration).

test_steps.action: Simulate a temperature deviation that triggers an alarm condition (e.g., by adjusting a sensor or simulating a fault).
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm is triggered by the system.
data_to_capture: Timestamp of alarm trigger.
Screenshot of alarm notification within the system.

test_steps.action: Measure the time from alarm trigger to the system's response (e.g., notification sent, alarm displayed prominently).
test_steps.expected_result: The system response time for the alarm condition does not exceed 30 seconds.
data_to_capture: Timestamp of alarm notification/display.
Calculated response time.

test_steps.action: Verify that the alarm notification is received by the designated personnel or system (e.g., paging system).
test_steps.expected_result: The alarm notification is successfully delivered to the intended recipient or system.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of notification receipt.

acceptance_criteria: System availability is at least 99.5% (excluding planned maintenance).
System response time for alarm conditions is within 30 seconds.
Alarm notifications are successfully generated and delivered.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-011: System response time shall not exceed 30 seconds for alarm conditions.
URS-EMS-013: System availability shall be 99.5% excluding planned maintenance.
data_integrity_requirements: Accurate logging of system uptime and downtime.
Precise timestamping of alarm events and system responses.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Vendor-Supplied Software Integrity and Unmodified State
test_cases.objective: To verify that the Environmental Monitoring System utilizes vendor-supplied software without any unauthorized modifications.
prerequisites: Access to the EMS system's software installation files or a method to verify software integrity.
Documentation of the vendor-supplied software version.

test_steps.action: Obtain the checksum (e.g., MD5, SHA-256) of the installed EMS software components.
test_steps.expected_result: Checksums for all installed software components are successfully generated.
data_to_capture: Checksums of installed software components.

test_steps.action: Compare the generated checksums with the checksums provided by the vendor for the specific software version.
test_steps.expected_result: All generated checksums match the vendor-provided checksums, confirming the software has not been modified.
data_to_capture: Comparison results of checksums.
Vendor-provided checksums.

acceptance_criteria: The checksums of the installed EMS software components match the vendor-provided checksums for the approved version.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-003: The system shall use vendor-supplied software without modification.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure the integrity of the software used by the EMS to prevent unauthorized changes that could impact data accuracy or system functionality.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Data Storage Capacity for Minimum 10 Years
test_cases.objective: To verify that the Environmental Monitoring System has sufficient data storage capacity to support a minimum of 10 years of continuous monitoring data.
prerequisites: Access to system logs and storage utilization reports.
Knowledge of the expected data generation rate (e.g., readings per sensor per day).
Information on the current storage allocation for the EMS database.

test_steps.action: Calculate the estimated total data volume generated per day based on the number of sensors, monitoring intervals, and data points stored per reading.
test_steps.expected_result: A clear calculation of daily data volume is documented.
data_to_capture: Number of sensors.
Monitoring interval (URS-EMS-002).
Data points per reading.
Calculated daily data volume.

test_steps.action: Project the total data volume over 10 years (3650 days) based on the calculated daily data volume.
test_steps.expected_result: A projected 10-year data volume is calculated.
data_to_capture: Projected 10-year data volume.

test_steps.action: Verify the current available storage capacity allocated to the EMS database.
test_steps.expected_result: Current available storage capacity is documented.
data_to_capture: Current available storage capacity.

test_steps.action: Compare the projected 10-year data volume with the current available storage capacity, considering any planned storage expansion or archival strategies.
test_steps.expected_result: The current storage capacity is sufficient to accommodate the projected 10-year data volume, or a clear plan for expansion/archival is in place.
data_to_capture: Comparison result.
Details of any storage expansion plans.

acceptance_criteria: The current storage capacity is sufficient to store 10 years of continuous monitoring data, or a documented plan for storage expansion or effective archival is in place.
The system's data storage capacity meets or exceeds the requirement of URS-EMS-012.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-012: Data storage capacity shall support minimum 10 years of continuous monitoring.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure sufficient storage to prevent data loss due to capacity limitations, which could impact historical data availability for investigations and compliance.
